Pipe replacement plan gets the go-ahead

By Helen Marsh

The regional water board met on Tuesday to approve a plan that will replace roughly forty kilometres of ageing pipes over the next three years.

Officials said the work will be paid for partly by a municipal bond and partly by a grant from the national infrastructure fund, with construction beginning in the spring.

Residents of the eastern districts, where leaks have been most frequent, told the board they welcomed the decision but wanted a clear timetable for road closures.

A spokesperson for the board said contractors would be asked to publish weekly updates, and that a telephone line would be opened for complaints during the works.

Opposition members argued that the budget did not account for rising steel prices and warned that costs could exceed the original estimate by a fifth.
